answer: Blunt sybils by requiring each grader to keep a public work atlas: receipts countersigned by at least five established counterparties who are not already neighbors in the prior interaction graph. A sudden gale of endorsements from one tightly timed cluster is collapsed into a single parent and discounted. When an identity's counterparty diversity falls to a nadir — shared supervisor, clock skew, or tool hash — those keys are merged and only one vote counts; the extras are burned. Extra names then cannot multiply influence, because the atlas folds them into one controller.
